method.description: Re-tested the recorded automated-retrieval block against every assigned official endpoint, then established each document's identity, issuer, role, revision and scope from the issuer's own published forms index. Because www.mass.gov refuses automated agents outright, the index was read from an official archived capture of that exact page, and the Massachusetts Trial Court's separate interactive-forms host was probed directly. No binary was retrieved, deposited, materialized or committed; no receipt was written; no third-party mirror was treated as authority.
method.attendedRetrievalPerformedNote: No human-in-browser retrieval was available to this worker. Every retrieval attempt recorded here is automated, and each is reported as an access fact.
method.binaryDeposition: No binary was retrieved or deposited. This job's ownedPaths are limited to this single production-factory JSON file.
method.byteVerificationNote: No SHA-256 in this record was measured in this job. The digests reproduced below are the values the source-artifact registry already carries for the held repository copies. Where a held copy's byte count is compared to the size the issuer publishes on its index, that agreement is corroboration of identity only; it is not a byte proof and does not clear any source gate.

dispositionDistinction.publicOfficialDocumentEvidence: All six assigned acquisitions resolve to forms published free, without login and without fee, on the Massachusetts Court System's official index 'Court forms for criminal records' at https://www.mass.gov/lists/court-forms-for-criminal-records, under the two headings 'Sealing criminal records' and 'Expunging criminal records'.
dispositionDistinction.automatedRetrievalBlockedNote: The recorded block reproduced, and it is broader today than when it was recorded. See automationBlockRetest.
dispositionDistinction.attendedOfficialRetrievalNote: Every one of these binaries requires a human-in-browser retrieval from www.mass.gov, or in the case of the Massachusetts Probation Service petition an interaction with the Trial Court's interactive XFA form host. This worker could not perform one and did not simulate one.
dispositionDistinction.sourceAbsentNote: Explicitly not absent, and must not be relabelled as missing, unavailable or unidentified. Every document is published, its issuer is confirmed, and five of six carry a revision confirmed against the issuer's own index. The obstacle is a delivery-channel refusal to scripted agents, nothing about the documents themselves.

automationBlockRetest.recordedStatus: BLOCKED — mass.gov HTML pages retrievable with full browser headers, but every /doc/…/download endpoint returns HTTP 403 to automated agents on both GET and HEAD across five endpoints tested (recorded 2026-08-03).
automationBlockRetest.agent: curl, Chrome 126 user-agent string, browser Accept header, redirects followed, 25s timeout
automationBlockRetest.conclusion: The block reproduces and has widened. On 2026-08-03 the HTML pages on www.mass.gov were retrievable and only the /doc/…/download endpoints refused; on 2026-08-07 the official index page itself returns 403 to the same class of agent. Six of six www.mass.gov endpoints refused. The refusal is host-scoped to www.mass.gov, not Commonwealth-wide: the Massachusetts Trial Court's own form host, courtforms.jud.state.ma.us, answered 200 to the identical agent.
automationBlockRetest.userAgentEvasionNote: A browser user-agent string was sent because that is the condition under which the original block was recorded, so the retest had to match it. No cookie, referer, CAPTCHA or WAF-token workaround was attempted, and none should be. The 403 is a publisher control and this job treats it as a boundary, not an obstacle to defeat.
automationBlockRetest.cautionAgainstOvergeneralising: A 403 is an access fact about this agent, from this network, on this date. It is not evidence that a document is missing, withdrawn, restricted, licensed or superseded, and it must not be converted into any of those findings. Nothing here says a human in a browser cannot download these forms; the acquisition record for every one of them says a human can.

The MPS Petition to Expunge (PROB0002, §§ 100F/100G/100H, time-based) is an administrative petition mailed to the Commissioner of Probation. The Trial Court Petition for Expungement (§ 100K, non-time-based) is a court filing. Different issuer, different statute, different filing route, different track (ma-expunge-time vs ma-expunge-k). They must never be interchanged, and a packet that files one where the other belongs is filed in the wrong forum.

questionsResolved.question: Do these forms exist and are they publicly published?
questionsResolved.answer: Yes. All six assigned acquisitions resolve to five distinct documents published free on the Commonwealth's official criminal-records forms index; the sixth is a selection within one of them.

questionsResolved.question: Who issues them?
questionsResolved.answer: Two issuers. The Massachusetts Probation Service, Office of the Commissioner of Probation, issues the Petition to Seal Form and the Petition to Expunge Form. The Executive Office of the Trial Court issues the Petition for Expungement Form, TC0021 and TC0057.

questionsResolved.question: Are they statewide or local?
questionsResolved.answer: Statewide, all of them. The Trial Court forms are standardized across the Boston Municipal, District, Juvenile and Superior Court departments; the Probation Service forms are furnished by the Commissioner for the whole Commonwealth.

questionsResolved.question: What is the current revision?
questionsResolved.answer: Confirmed from the issuer's own index for five: Petition to Seal 4/12; Petition to Expunge 10/11/18; Petition for Expungement 12/20/18; Marijuana Expungement 11/8/22; TC0057 Rev. 3/24. TC0057's index revision cannot be reconciled with the held copy — see its revisionConflictUnresolved.
